subject.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args

question: Should the cron agent tool permanently accept and repair scalar `toolsAllow` and `fallbacks` values while advertising flat provider-routing fields to models?
rationale: Tests and installed proof establish that the mechanism works, but they cannot decide whether converting malformed model output into accepted tool permissions and provider routing is the intended long-term security and model-facing contract.

options.title: Approve the bounded repair contract
options.body: Accept the flat fields and exact single-string-to-array coercion because shell fields remain rejected and downstream cron/provider authorization is unchanged.

options.title: Keep security-sensitive arrays strict
options.body: Expose the flat cron fields but require `toolsAllow` and `fallbacks` to remain arrays so malformed security/provider arguments continue to fail validation.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded repair contract
recommendation.body: Accept the flat fields and exact single-string-to-array coercion because shell fields remain rejected and downstream cron/provider authorization is unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged cron compatibility sweep is the strongest available history signal for the schema and runtime boundary affected by this choice.
